post_title: 6.5% cap rate, 1.8% return. Cap rate vs cash-on-cash, explained.
example: Example numbers for illustration · 25% down · 7% · 30-year loan

lines.voice: Six and a half percent cap rate. One point eight percent return. Same house. Here's why.
Cap rate starts with *N O I*: yearly rent, minus operating costs. {Thirty thousand|$30,000}, minus {ten five|$10,500}, is {nineteen five|$19,500}.
Divide by the price, {three hundred thousand|$300,000}. That's a {six and a half percent|6.5%} cap rate, as if you paid cash.
But you have a loan. Subtract the mortgage, {seventeen nine sixty-four|$17,964}, and you keep {fifteen thirty-six|$1,536} a year.
Divide by the cash you put in, {eighty-four thousand|$84,000}. Cash-on-cash: {one point eight percent|1.8%}.

visual.text: Cap rate rates the *property.* Cash-on-cash rates *your deal.*

lines.voice: Cap rate rates the property. Cash-on-cash rates your deal.
DealCaddie shows both on any listing. We read the greens. You take the shot.

caption:
6.5% cap rate. 1.8% return. Same house.

Cap rate = NOI ÷ price. It rates the property as if you paid cash.
$30,000 rent − $10,500 operating costs = $19,500 NOI
$19,500 ÷ $300,000 = 6.5%

Cash-on-cash = yearly cash flow ÷ cash you put in. It rates YOUR deal, loan included.
$19,500 − $17,964 mortgage = $1,536/yr
$1,536 ÷ $84,000 (down + closing) = 1.8%

Example numbers for illustration (25% down, 7%, 30 yr).
